question: A can do a work in 16 days and B can do the same work in 18 days. If they work on it together for 4 days, then what fraction of the work is left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 16 and 18 = 144 units.

Combined efficiency of A and B = (144 ÷ 16) + (144 ÷ 18) = 9 + 8 = 17 units/day.

Work completed in 4 days together = 17 × 4 = 68 units.

Remaining work = 144 − 68 = 76 units.

Fraction of work left = 76 ÷ 144 = 19/36.

**∴ The correct answer is 19/36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 16 days

Time taken by B = 18 days

Days worked together = 4 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 9 + 8 = 17 units/day

⇒ Total work completed in 4 days = 17 × 4 = 68 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work completed

⇒ Remaining work = 144 − 68 = 76 units

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining work ÷ Total work

⇒ Fraction of work left = 76 / 144

⇒ Fraction of work left = 19/36

**∴ The correct answer is 19/36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person. If people work for the exact same number of days, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

If A and B work on alternate days starting with A, then the total work done in a 2-day cycle equals the sum of their individual daily efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The underlying concept is identical to Time & Work. An inlet pipe has positive efficiency (filling the tank), while an outlet pipe or leak has negative efficiency (emptying the tank).
